T: Never sick. Never hurt. Always hungry.
D: The sole survivor of a train crash learns from a fragile comic book collector that he may be a real superhero.
P: Serve the mains when David sits down to breakfast with his son Joseph.
S: Homemade soft pretzels dipped in bicarb water, topped with rock salt
Soft pretzels boiled in bicarb water, rock salt on top, baked at 220C for 12 minutes, with yellow mustard.
a Philadelphia breakfast before the stadium shift

Pork, sage and polenta set into a loaf, sliced and fried until crunchy outside and soft inside, with apple butter and a fried egg. Brown 500g pork mince with 1 diced onion, then add 1L chicken stock, 1 tsp dried sage, 1/2 tsp pepper and salt and bring to the boil. Whisk in 180g polenta and stir over low heat for 15 minutes until very thick. Press into a lined loaf tin and chill overnight. Slice 1.5cm thick, dust with flour and fry in butter for 4 minutes a side until crisp. Serve with apple butter and fried eggs.
Paper thin purple sweet potato fried crisp

Purple sweet potatoes sliced paper thin and fried until crisp, dusted with sea salt and smoked paprika, as purple as Elijah's suits. Slice 2 purple sweet potatoes paper thin on a mandoline and soak in cold water for 20 minutes. Drain and dry very well on tea towels. Fry in small batches in oil at 160C for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the bubbling slows and they crisp up. Drain on paper towel and season straight away with sea salt and a pinch of smoked paprika. Cool so they crisp fully.
M: Dunn family bacon and scrambled eggs
David, Audrey and Joseph at the kitchen table

Soft buttery scrambled eggs with chives, crisp bacon, grilled tomatoes and thick buttered toast, served family style at the kitchen table. Fry 8 bacon rashers until crisp and keep warm. Halve 4 tomatoes, season and grill cut side up for 5 minutes. Whisk 8 eggs with 60ml milk and salt. Melt 30g butter in a non-stick pan over low heat, add the eggs and stir slowly for 4 minutes until just set and creamy, then stir in chopped chives. Toast 4 thick slices of bread and butter well. Serve with orange juice.
Weight room rump with garlic butter
Rump steaks with parsley garlic butter and roast potatoes

Thick rump steaks grilled to medium and topped with melting garlic and parsley butter, with crunchy roast potatoes and buttered green beans. Roast 1kg potato chunks tossed in oil and salt at 220C for 45 minutes. Mash 80g soft butter with 2 crushed garlic cloves and chopped parsley. Season 4 x 250g rump steaks and grill over high heat for 4 minutes a side for medium, then rest 5 minutes. Blanch 300g green beans for 3 minutes and toss with a little butter. Top each steak with a slice of the garlic butter.
W: Mr Glass lemon and berry jelly
Lemon jelly set with blueberries and raspberries

Lemon juice and sugar warmed with gelatine until dissolved, poured into round glasses over blueberries and raspberries, set for 4 hours until clear. Warm 500ml water with the juice of 3 lemons and 120g sugar. Soak 5 gelatine sheets, squeeze and stir in until dissolved. Divide 125g blueberries and 125g raspberries among round glasses and pour over the jelly. Chill for 4 hours until clear and set.
K: Fresh ginger simmered, then steeped with green tea and honey

Hot green tea steeped with fresh ginger, sweetened with honey and sharpened with lemon, with a splash of whisky for anyone who wants it. Simmer a 5cm piece of sliced ginger in 1L water for 5 minutes, then take off the heat and let it cool for 2 minutes. Add 4 green tea bags and steep for 3 minutes, then remove. Stir in 4 tbsp honey and the juice of 1 lemon. Pour into 4 mugs with a lemon slice each. Add 30ml whisky to any mug where it's wanted.
